- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment; model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative; model fails to adjust downward in low-sentiment periods.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to recent price drops or sentiment shifts, especially in the first 3–5 days of a new trend.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to over- or under-forecasting in the middle of the 30-day horizon.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is >0.3, model tends to overreact; when sentiment <0.2, model underreacts — adjust forecast magnitude based on sentiment intensity.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast are most prone to error; model often misjudges short-term volatility near the end of the 30-day window.
